gold_source: Authored by Claude (this session) as a structural replica of entity-case1 with new surface content, to begin building n>1 for the recency-vs-verb-semantics competition pattern. Not yet independently reviewed or piloted — treat any score against it as illustrative, not a finding, until reviewed (see reference/experiment-plan-symmetric.md §1).
prompt:
You will read a short workplace conversation between two colleagues, then answer one question about the final message. Do not explain your uncertainty away — if more than one file genuinely fits, say so.

Turn 1 — Colleague: "Can you get invoice-march.pdf ready to send to Priya?"
Turn 2 — You: "Sure."
Turn 3 — Colleague: "Also, take a look at invoice-march-revised.pdf."
Turn 4 — You: "OK."
Turn 5 — Colleague: "And invoice-march-final.pdf needs attention too."
Turn 6 — You: "Noted."
Turn 7 — Colleague: "Go ahead and send it to Priya."

Question: which file (by exact filename) does Turn 7 instruct you to send, and to whom? If you genuinely cannot tell, say so explicitly instead of guessing.

End your answer with a single JSON object on its own line: {"entity": "<filename or 'cannot_determine'>", "recipient": "<name or 'cannot_determine'>", "confidence": "<low|medium|high>"}

metadata.description: Structural replica of entity-case1 (invoice domain instead of report domain). Recency (invoice-march-final.pdf) competes against verb-semantic binding (invoice-march.pdf, the only file tied to 'send' in Turn 1).
